title: One-on-One prep: bridge cadences and growth check
agenda: Progress on Q4 micro-OKR: batching optimizations (10m)
Career gateway check: readiness for L4->L5 expectations (10m)
Manager asks: roadmap alignment, risk to release (5m)
Open feedback & 1 action to close before next 1:1 (5m)
quick_updates: Ship window: target model-serving benchmark complete; perf numbers ~8% better median latency
PR #487 merged to staging but flaky in nightly (see linked PR).
Customer demo scheduled 2026-11-03 — need predictable latency for 99th p90 SLOs
Hiring: SRE candidate interview Thursday; their notes below
notes:
Purpose: make this 1:1 concrete and outcome-oriented. I want to leave with 1 clear action for Tejas and 1 for me. Keep the conversation pragmatic: metrics + career + blockers.

Pulse check starters: energy 1-5, main focus for week, one thing to deprioritize.

On batching micro-OKR: remind them that reducing small-req tail latencies is higher priority than absolute average token throughput for the demo. Suggest experiment: reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 12 -> 6 for canary and measure tail and cost. If tail improves without >7% cost increase, roll-forward.

Career checkpoint: ask for concrete examples aligned to L5 rubric: cross-team influence, tradeoff ownership, mentorship evidence. I will give specific feedback (3 examples) and ask them to pick 2 coachable behaviors to work on.

Blocker deep-dive: infra quota — contact infra-ops (Dylan) to escalate GPU quota request (state why customer demo is time-sensitive). Test flakiness: capture one reproducible failure and open an experiment branch that runs the failing test with extra logging. Offer pairing time this week (30m) to root cause.
concerns_and_risks: Nightly flakiness could block demo if not mitigated — risk level: medium-high
If we tighten batching too aggressively, cost spike could force rollback before demo
Candidate pipeline: if SRE hire slips, oncall bandwidth stretched for next three sprints
coaching_prompts: Give me a recent example where you influenced another team to change infra defaults — what worked?
Describe a time you had to balance quality vs. shipping quickly; what signals did you use?
Which two skills would you like concrete coaching on this quarter?
action_items: Tejas: run canary with max_batch_wait_ms=6 on staging by 2026-10-25, report p50/p90/p99 and cost delta
Tejas: prepare 2 L5-aligned examples for next 1:1 (mentorship + cross-team impact) by 2026-11-03
Me (Tejas): pair with Dylan for 30m to triage flaky test and capture reproducible steps by 2026-10-27
Me (manager): escalate GPU quota request to infra-ops with subject 'Customer demo 2026-11-03 — temporary quota bump' by 2026-10-22
Hiring: share interview feedback for SRE candidate with recruiting by 2026-10-23 (owner: Maya Kapoor)
Document: add a short troubleshooting checklist to PR #487 describing how to run the failing job locally (owner: Tejas)
followups: Confirm staging canary telemetry is wired to console route for quick dashboarding
Check that recruiting updates candidate pipeline and next-round interview is scheduled
Verify customer demo runbook includes fallback to older model variant if tail latency regresses
personal_reflection: I tend to jump into technical fixes; remind myself to prioritize coaching behavior over immediate code changes. In the 1:1, ask one open question and then listen 70% of the time. Leave room for the report to propose their own mitigations.
